headline: World's First Stored-Program Computer Executes Its Initial Run in Manchester
dispatch: The machine known as the Manchester Baby completed its first successful stored-program run at Victoria University of Manchester on June 21, 1948. Engineers Freddie Williams and Tom Kilburn had loaded the program onto the cathode-ray tube memory and watched as the small experimental computer worked through its calculations. The milestone marks the first time a full program was held in electronic memory and executed by a machine without human intervention at each step.
answer: Manchester Baby runs world's first stored-program, 1948
